title: Load only the active UI surface and avoid duplicate startup refresh
goal: Reduce launch and screen-transition work by removing repeated startup refreshes, deferring local model residency until Chat is opened, and avoiding a full catalog refresh after model preparation.
context: The app previously refreshed the session in both PersonalAgentApp.initialize and RootView.task. RootView also prepared the active model immediately, and prepareActiveModel used run(_:), which refreshes all catalogs after loading. This stacks model loading and broad state updates into startup. RootView should own one observational refresh; ChatScreen should request model preparation only when it is presented; preparation must update only model lifecycle/error state.
forbidden_changes: Do not change Agent visual design or navigation behavior.
Do not alter Kernel, provider, model-loading, or persistence contracts.
Do not change Skill execution, security policy, or verification behavior.
Do not claim measured performance gains without launch-time measurements.
acceptance_criteria: PersonalAgentApp assigns the session without running a second refresh or model preparation.
RootView performs one session refresh and does not load the local model during initial app launch.
Opening Chat triggers local model preparation, but repeated visits do not reload an already loaded model.
Model preparation does not call the broad run(_:)/refresh path or reload unrelated catalogs.
Cancellation remains non-fatal; real model-load errors remain visible.
Agent Task Contract, M3, and Apple Native Build & Unsigned IPA pass on the final PR head.
Startup latency and physical-device behavior remain explicitly unmeasured unless device evidence is collected.
verification: Confirm Agent Task Contract, M3, and Apple Native Build & Unsigned IPA pass on the final PR head.
On iPhone, compare cold launch and first-chat readiness before/after if device access is available.
recovery: Revert the single squashed task commit if deferred model preparation breaks local chat startup; restore preparation at the chat boundary rather than app launch.
